title: Reciprocal eigenvalues
statement:
In the Poincare duality conventions [def-pod-conventions] of this chapter (the fixed setting), let $(K,\varphi_K)$ be a strict Weil complex with $K$ perfect, at a *field* coefficient stage $\Lambda \in \{ E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }\}$ (the hypothesis of [thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field]; the statement fails over $\mathcal O_E$, where the degreewise pairing need not be perfect). Relative to the perfect pairing of [thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field], the operator $F_{K^\vee }$ on $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )$ is conjugate to

$$
q^d\, \bigl(F_{c,K}^{-1}\bigr)^{\mathsf t}.
$$

Thus an eigenvalue $\alpha$ of $F_{c,K}$ on $H_c^i(X,K)$ with algebraic multiplicity $m$ corresponds, with the same multiplicity, to the eigenvalue $q^d/\alpha$ of $F_{K^\vee }$ on $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )$. If $X_0$ is proper, the first space is $H^i(X,K)$. Here eigenvalues at the $E$ stage are computed in the fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and algebraic multiplicity means multiplicity as a root of the characteristic polynomial [def-weil-characteristic-polynomial, def-weil-root-multiplicity]. The scalar-valued adjoint is obtained by choosing a trivialization of the value line $\Lambda(-d)$; equivalently, the conjugacy is intrinsically with the dual tensored with that line.

proof.text: Put $V=H_c^i(X,K)$, $W=H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee)$ and $L=\Lambda(-d)$. By [thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field], $V,W$ are finite-dimensional and the line-valued pairing $b_L:V\times W\to L$ is perfect. Choose a nonzero vector in the one-dimensional coefficient line $L$, hence a linear isomorphism $t:L\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda$. Then $b=t\circ b_L$ is perfect: composing either adjoint with the isomorphism induced by $t$ preserves bijectivity. Thus $\Phi:W\xrightarrow{\sim}V^\vee$, $\Phi(y)(x)=b(x,y)$, is an isomorphism. This uses the ordinary finite-dimensional dual explicitly supplied by the cited field-stage theorem, not a claim about integral degreewise duals.

source.place: Proof, Step 1; explicit linear algebra and proper-operator compatibility as detailed here

proof.text: Write $F=F_{c,K}$, $G=F_{K^\vee}$ and $c=q^d\in\Lambda$. The Tate datum [def-pur-tate-datum] states that $q$ is a unit at all coefficient stages, so $c\ne0$ in our field. By [cor-pod-untwisted-similitude], $b_L(Fx,Gy)=q^db_L(x,y)$. Applying the linear map $t$ gives $b(Fx,Gy)=c\,b(x,y)$ for all $x,y$. In particular the two finite-dimensional spaces, the scalar-valued perfect pairing, and the nonzero multiplier satisfy every hypothesis of [lem-weil-similitude-pairing-reciprocity].

source.place: Proof, Step 2; explicit linear algebra and proper-operator compatibility as detailed here

proof.text: Clause 2 of [lem-weil-similitude-pairing-reciprocity] implies that $F$ and $G$ are invertible. For $x\in V,y\in W$, substitute $F^{-1}x$ into the identity of step 2 to obtain $\Phi(Gy)(x)=b(x,Gy)=c\,b(F^{-1}x,y)=\bigl(c(F^{-1})^{\mathsf t}\Phi(y)\bigr)(x)$. Equality of these functionals for every $x$ proves $\Phi G=c(F^{-1})^{\mathsf t}\Phi$, hence $\Phi G\Phi^{-1}=c(F^{-1})^{\mathsf t}$. This is the required conjugacy, with its specified adjoint. A different trivialization multiplies $\Phi$ by a nonzero scalar, which cancels in this displayed conjugation.

source.place: Proof, Step 3; explicit linear algebra and proper-operator compatibility as detailed here

proof.text: Apply clause 4 of [lem-weil-similitude-pairing-reciprocity] to the data checked in steps 1 and 2, using the inclusion $\Lambda\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ (the identity at the algebraically closed stage). It says that the eigenvalue multiset of $G$ is the image of that of $F$ under $\alpha\mapsto q^d/\alpha$, counted with algebraic multiplicity. Invertibility excludes $\alpha=0$. Since $c\ne0$, equality $c/\alpha=c/\alpha^\prime$ for nonzero $\alpha,\alpha^\prime$ implies $\alpha=\alpha^\prime$ by multiplying by $\alpha\alpha^\prime$ and cancelling $c$. Therefore an eigenvalue of multiplicity $m$ contributes exactly multiplicity $m$, without merging distinct eigenvalues.

source.place: Proof, Step 4; explicit linear algebra and proper-operator compatibility as detailed here

proof.text: If $X_0$ is proper, [thm-pod-proper-poincare-duality] supplies the canonical comparison $R\Gamma_c(X,K)\cong R\Gamma(X,K)$, hence $V\cong H^i(X,K)$. It also identifies the Poincare pairing under this comparison. For completeness the comparison respects the operators: write $\kappa_M$ for its derived version and use the identity compactification as in [lem-pod-proper-coincidence-frobenius]. That node gives $\tau_K\kappa_K=\kappa_{Lg^*K}\tau_{c,K}$ and says that $\kappa$ is natural in $M$. Naturality for $\varphi_K:Lg^*K\to K$ gives $R\Gamma(\varphi_K)\kappa_{Lg^*K}=\kappa_KR\Gamma_c(\varphi_K)$. Substitution into the definitions of $F_K,F_{c,K}$ in [def-pod-conventions] yields $F_K\kappa_K=\kappa_KF_{c,K}$. Taking degree $i$ proves that the first space and its Frobenius may be replaced by ordinary cohomology.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), let $(K,\varphi_K)$ be a strict Weil complex with $K$ perfect, at a *field* coefficient stage $\Lambda \in \{ E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }\}$ (the hypothesis of [thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field]; the statement fails over $\mathcal O_E$, where the degreewise pairing need not be perfect). Relative to the perfect pairing of [thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field], the operator $F_{K^\vee }$ on $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )$ is conjugate to

$$
q^d\, \bigl(F_{c,K}^{-1}\bigr)^{\mathsf t}.
$$

Thus an eigenvalue $\alpha$ of $F_{c,K}$ on $H_c^i(X,K)$ with algebraic multiplicity $m$ corresponds, with the same multiplicity, to the eigenvalue $q^d/\alpha$ of $F_{K^\vee }$ on $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )$. If $X_0$ is proper, the first space is $H^i(X,K)$.

proof.text:
Step 1: the adjoint identification. By [thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field] the degreewise pairing is perfect, so the bilinear form $b:H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )\to \Lambda$ is nondegenerate and the map

$$
\Phi :H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )\longrightarrow H_c^i(X,K)^\vee , \qquad \Phi (y)(x)=\langle x,y\rangle ^{\mathrm{untw}}_i,
$$

is an isomorphism of $\Lambda$-vector spaces, the field-stage dual being the ordinary dual, by [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Step 2: the similitude translates. The untwisted similitude of [cor-pod-untwisted-similitude], $b(F_{c,K}x,F_{K^\vee }y)=q^db(x,y)$, says precisely that

$$
\Phi \circ F_{K^\vee }=q^d\, \bigl(F_{c,K}^{-1}\bigr)^{\mathsf t}\circ \Phi ,
$$

where $\bigl(F_{c,K}^{-1}\bigr)^{\mathsf t}$ is the transpose of the inverse operator on the dual $H_c^i(X,K)^\vee$. Therefore $F_{K^\vee }=q^d\Phi ^{-1}\bigl(F_{c,K}^{-1}\bigr)^{\mathsf t}\Phi$, i.e. $F_{K^\vee }$ is conjugate to $q^d\bigl(F_{c,K}^{-1}\bigr)^{\mathsf t}$. Step 3: eigenvalues. A linear operator on a finite-dimensional vector space and its transpose have the same characteristic polynomial, and conjugation does not change it, so the eigenvalues of $F_{K^\vee }$ are the eigenvalues of $q^dF_{c,K}^{-1}$; on the finite-dimensional space $H_c^i(X,K)$ (Step 1 and the finite-dimensionality of [thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field]) the eigenvalues of an automorphism are the inverses of the eigenvalues of the operator, each with the same algebraic multiplicity, so the eigenvalues of $F_{K^\vee }$ are the $q^d/\alpha$ with the multiplicities of the eigenvalues $\alpha$ of $F_{c,K}$. Step 4: the last assertion is the proper comparison $H_c^i=H^i$ of [thm-pod-proper-poincare-duality], which requires $X_0$ proper.
